title: FPS almost halved going from 4.4 dev3 to 4.4 dev4 in a Forward+ 2D project
body: I can reproduce a major FPS drop in Godot 4.4 dev4 on Windows 10 with Vulkan Forward+ and an RTX 4090. In the same 2D game scenario, the editor drops from about 383 FPS in dev3 to 200 FPS in dev4, and the exported game drops from about 402 FPS to 240 FPS. The project makes heavy use of RenderingServer. I have not reproduced this in a new empty scene and do not yet have a minimal reproduction project.

symptoms_visible: In the same 2D game scenario, editor performance drops from about 383 FPS in dev3 to 200 FPS in dev4, while the exported game drops from about 402 FPS to 240 FPS.
N0.label: N0 severe dev4 FPS regression reported

symptoms_visible: The dev4 profiler is slower in the same loaded game state, and the remote scene tree is extremely slow.
The version-to-version FPS gap appears with Forward+; Compatibility remains consistent between dev3 and dev4.
Removing the individual texture-rectangle draws or disabling light shadows brings the two versions much closer together, while merely hiding the scene content does not.
N1.label: N1 regression isolated to Forward+ texture and shadow workload

symptoms_visible: Dev2 runs at about 384 FPS, essentially the same as dev3.
Scenes with few objects or walls drawn from atlas regions stay similar between versions, but adding many separately textured objects or lights produces a large gap.
N2.label: N2 regression range and workload pattern measured

symptoms_visible: Increasing the uniform-set cache improves dev4 from roughly 256 FPS to about 300 FPS, but dev3 still runs around 390 FPS.
Values above 512, including values as high as 50000, do not raise dev4 above roughly 300 FPS.
N2_x.label: N2_x cache-size increase aftermath

symptoms_visible: CPU usage remains around 8% in both dev3 and dev4.
With the cache set to 512 or higher, disabling light shadows makes the FPS roughly equal between the builds; enabling shadows restores the performance gap.
N3.label: N3 shadow-heavy project available for profiling

symptoms_visible: The provided candidate branch reaches about 345 FPS in my self-compiled build, compared with about 300 FPS in dev4, although I cannot compare it directly with an equivalently optimized official build.
N4.label: N4 shadow draw-list candidate tested

symptoms_visible: In the later dev7 build, the same scene runs at about 295 FPS rather than the roughly 390 FPS I still get in dev3.
N4_x.label: N4_x shadow draw-list optimization aftermath

symptoms_visible: After compiling the latest master containing the thread-guard performance change, the same scene runs at around 615 FPS.
N_terminal.label: terminal performance regression resolved

question_patterns: Can you compare profiler captures from the two builds in exactly the same game state?
What parts of the editor or profiler become slower in dev4?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured the debug profilers one after the other in the same loaded level. Dev4 is on the left and dev3 on the right in the attached comparisons. The remote scene tree is also extremely slow in dev4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The profiler values fluctuate slightly, but dev4 remains substantially slower in repeated captures of the same scene.

question_patterns: Does hiding or removing visible scene content change the version-to-version gap?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I managed to hide everything in the dev4 scene, but it did not seem to make a difference.

question_patterns: Does this also happen with the Compatibility renderer, or only with Forward+?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It only happens with Forward+. Compatibility keeps the frames consistent across dev3 and dev4 in every case I tried, although Compatibility is slower when lights are used.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same proportional drop occurs with Compatibility and Forward+ and also with a blank scene.

question_patterns: Can you disable parts of the RenderingServer workload to see what makes the gap disappear?
Do textures, lights, or shadows have a measurable effect on the regression?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Commenting out my canvas_item_add_texture_rect calls or turning off shadows for the lights keeps the project at roughly the same FPS in both versions. Hiding the background, particles, and GUI does not make much difference.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Disabling every light, shadow, and texture draw leaves exactly the same dev3-to-dev4 gap.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c1, c4, and c6: produno supplied side-by-side profiler captures and progressively isolated the behavior to the Forward+ path, individual texture draws, and light shadows. No other participant's setup is merged here.

question_patterns: Can you bisect between the last fast development build and the first slow one and paste the raw result?
What commit or range does the regression bisection print?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The bisection gave me commit 0d1d94572750b624e10aa6e655011e37028fa1c5, titled '2D: Fix various issues and minor performance optimisations'. The best build I reached during the run was around 335 FPS, although I was not compiling for production use.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection shows the slowdown was already present before dev3, with no 2D rendering changes in the final range.
The same commit is printed, but my unoptimized bisection build runs a few FPS slower.

question_patterns: Can you test dev2, from before the canvas batching changes, in the same scene?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Dev2 gives me around 384 FPS, pretty much the same as dev3. The attached image is the 2D scene I am rendering.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Dev2 is also around 250 FPS, the same as dev4.

question_patterns: When you remove those texture-rectangle calls, are you replacing them or simply rendering fewer objects?
How does the result change between a sparse scene and one filled with atlas-region draws?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am rendering fewer objects. A new game with few objects has roughly the same FPS in both versions. Filling the space with walls drawn from sprite-sheet regions using canvas_item_add_texture_rect_region also keeps the versions close.

question_patterns: Which object or texture arrangement makes the slowdown become large?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The large difference appears when I add more objects through canvas_item_add_texture_rect using mostly singular textures, or when I add lights. Atlas-region wall draws do not produce the same version gap.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A single atlas-region wall produces the full slowdown, while hundreds of separate textures and lights do not change it.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c9, c12, and c20-c22: produno ran the requested bisection and dev2 comparison, then described raw workload observations. The commit identity is present in the reporter's bisection output; later causal interpretation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Treat uniform-set cache thrashing as the whole regression and increase the 2D batching uniform-set cache until all unique textures fit.
solution.concrete_example: Raise rendering/2d/batching/uniform_set_cache_size from its default to 512, 2048, or a much larger value and compare the same scene.

edges.comment: Maintainer suggestions c7, c19 and reporter results c9, c20, c35: larger cache values improve one component but plateau around 300 FPS and do not restore the roughly 390 FPS dev3 result. It is therefore falsified as the complete resolution, not as a partial optimization.

question_patterns: Can you share the affected project privately so a maintainer can profile the exact workload?
Would you be able to arrange private access to the project rather than posting it publicly?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I arranged private access and shared the full project so the same scene could be tested without publishing my codebase.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot share the project or produce any smaller workload that reproduces the regression.

question_patterns: Do you see a measurable difference in overall CPU usage between dev3 and dev4?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. Both stay around 8% CPU usage with the game open and running.

question_patterns: After raising the cache, can you retest with light shadows enabled and disabled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With the cache at 512, setting light shadows to false gives me roughly the same FPS in both builds. With shadows true, the large difference comes back.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The gap remains unchanged when every light shadow is disabled.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c24, c28, and c36: produno privately shared the original affected project, reported equal overall CPU utilization, and confirmed that shadows account for the remaining gap after the cache adjustment. Maintainer profiling results are not placed in the reporter's answer.

question_patterns: Can you test the provided candidate branch against the same saved scene and report the FPS?
Please compile and run this proposed performance branch, then compare it with your previous self-compiled result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am not sure how to compile with the same optimizations as the development builds, but this branch gives me about 345 FPS. During the earlier bisection I reached about 335 FPS, and dev4 was only around 300 FPS, so it looks better. I will need an official build for a direct comparison.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate branch remains at about 300 FPS, exactly the same as dev4.
The branch reaches about 340 FPS instead of 345 FPS under the same self-compiled setup.

edges.comment: Reporter c41 tested clayjohn's pre-landing candidate branch. This is a legitimate pre-landing build measurement; the reporter expressed uncertainty about compiler optimization and did not claim the issue was fully resolved.

solution.intent: Resolve the shadow-heavy regression by reducing the number of draw lists and RenderingDevice API calls used for PointLight2D shadow rendering.
solution.concrete_example: Batch the PointLight2D shadow work so each light no longer creates four unnecessary draw lists, then ship that optimization in a development build.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainer profiling linked a portion of the slowdown to the large number of draw lists and API calls created by PointLight2D shadows. The reporter supplied only the workload behavior and candidate-build FPS.

edges.comment: Maintainer analysis c37-c40 proposed reducing the shadow draw-list count. Reporter c42 later tested the landed result in dev7 and still measured about 295 FPS versus about 390 FPS in dev3, so this was a real partial improvement but not the final resolution.

solution.intent: Use a build containing the thread-guard performance optimization: the remaining regression is excessive thread-guard overhead amplified by the shadow-heavy RenderingDevice call pattern, rather than unresolved uniform-set cache capacity alone.
solution.concrete_example: Build or install a current development snapshot containing the thread-guard performance change, keep the cache at a reasonable value, and retest the original shadow-heavy scene with the same settings before declaring the regression fixed.
solution.inference_hint: The final accepted diagnosis came from maintainer profiling and the dramatic before/after result of the thread-guard performance change. The reporter established that shadows and Forward+ trigger the gap and that cache and draw-list changes were insufficient, but did not independently derive the thread-guard mechanism.

edges.comment: Maintainer c49 requested testing of the newly merged thread-guard performance change. Reporter c50 compiled latest master and observed about 615 FPS in the same scene; c51 accepted that change as the fix. The terminal confirmation is reporter-owned and occurred only after the change had landed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as excessive thread-guard overhead, amplified by the very large number of RenderingDevice calls in the project's PointLight2D shadow workload.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the regression is Forward+-specific, dev2/dev3 are fast, disabling shadows removes the remaining gap, and the affected project was reproduced and profiled.
Must not present increasing the 2D uniform-set cache as the complete fix; it improved performance but plateaued well below dev3 in the reporter's scene.
Must not present reducing PointLight2D shadow draw lists as the complete fix; the landed change improved performance but dev7 still remained substantially below dev3 for the reporter.
Must recommend testing a build containing the thread-guard performance change and must not declare resolution until the reporter verifies the original scene on that build.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Godot developer with a large, long-running 2D project. Comfortable using RenderingServer APIs, changing project settings, compiling engine branches, and running a first-time regression bisection, but unsure about matching official compiler optimizations.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and measurement-focused. Supplies repeated FPS comparisons and screenshots, openly notes uncertainty, protects proprietary project code but will share it privately, and challenges partial fixes with additional controlled tests.
